items.gist: The blissful liṅga is the yoginīhṛdaya; through seed-yoni union it produces consciousness, while Bhairava's contracted-expanded power renews the world by visarga ānanda.
The anuttara upāya is taught by resemblance; even without entering objects, the yogi knows the bliss of vṛtti-cessation and stands full-rayed in truth.
The uccāra method is stated, then karaṇa is distinguished as sevenfold practice preceded by knowledge, to be learned from the guru and explained further.
Varṇa is sound resembling the unmanifest and is the seed of creation and dissolution; repetition leads the yogi to cidātmatā, and memory reveals mantra-svarūpa.
Smṛti generates svarūpa and colors all states; bija piṇḍas without convention still stir consciousness, while prāṇa processes complete them.
First saṃvedana is touch; the fourteenth entry unifies the self, then visarga uccāra leads both dvādaśānta paths with the heart, and kanda-to-kuṇḍalinī processes bring the seed.
By this method the wise quickly enters the supreme dhāma; varṇa as colors or post-initiation forms is contemplated, and the bindu shines like a spark, producing tādātmya.
This is an upalakṣaṇa for all mantras; through excess of saṃvid, physical varṇa-jāla becomes non-physical, and gurus display varied methods through uccāra, karaṇa, dhyāna, and varṇa.

The sequence for attaining the anuttara pada is given; skipping is for the superior yogi, while gradual practice is for the dull, and the anuttara upāya is finally declared as the external clear path.
